gap: No result ChatGPT got puts today's maker-store prices for the music speakers next to the speakerphones: the Tribit StormBox Micro 3 is $64.99 on tribit.com, the same as the Avantree Roadtrip's $64.99 on avantree.com, and the soundcore Boom Go 3i is $79.99 on us.soundcore.com.
standout_why: I compared against itechguides (prices the Roadtrip at $64.99, the CK11 at $44.99, the VeoPulse B-PRO 2B at $59.99, the Besign BK06 at $23.99 and the AGPTEK at $21.99, all as of 2026-11-16), carcody (Roadtrip $64.99, CK11 $44.99, Select 4 Go at $22.99 on promo or $34.99 regular, Emberton III about $129.99) and qualitreviews (has no prices at all and still lists the Jabra Drive with an Amazon link). The rivals already price the speakerphones and the Select 4 Go. What they lack is a price for the Tribit StormBox Micro 3 and the Boom Go 3i, and any sign that the Jabra Drive's US maker page is gone. Price does not decide this question, though. Function does: calls, playing music, or sending sound to the car stereo.
decides: This confirms the pick and does not change it. At $64.99 the shopper chooses between the Roadtrip (FM transmitter to the car stereo plus a visor speaker, 3 W ×2 and 8 h of music at 60% volume per itechguides) and the StormBox Micro 3 (a standalone music speaker) for the same money. So the choice is about how they'll use it, not cost. The $34.99 Select 4 Go is the budget floor but has only 5 W. The Jabra Drive row on our page should be checked or removed, because Jabra's US product URL returns 404.
